Q: Variable propagation between Yocto recipes - Best practices A:

Easiest answer of how to do this is create an app.inc that contains everything common to building the app and then creating a app-a.bb and app-b.bb which just include app.inc and set VAR1=value-a or value-b respectively. Then the images can install either app-a or app-b.

Q: Is JavaScript an open source programming language? A:

In addition to the answer given above, there is also an open source .NET implementation of JavaScript available: Its name is Jurassic, and it is available on CodePlex:

http://jurassic.codeplex.com/

Examples:

  1. Execute an expression:

    var engine = new Jurassic.ScriptEngine();

    Console.WriteLine(engine.Evaluate<int>("1.5 + 2.4"));

  2. Execute a script:

    var engine = new Jurassic.ScriptEngine();

    engine.ExecuteFile(@"c:\test.js");

Features of version 2.2 (taken from web site):

  • Supports all ECMAScript 3 and ECMAScript 5 functionality, including ES5 strict mode
  • Simple yet powerful API
  • Compiles JavaScript into .NET bytecode (CIL); not an interpreter
  • Deployed as a single .NET assembly (no native code)
  • Basic support for integrated debugging within Visual Studio
  • Uses light-weight code generation, so generated code is fully garbage collected
  • Tested on .NET 3.5, .NET 4 and Silverlight

Q: valgrind can not detect any leak A:

Copying a Valgrind installation to a different prefix is not supported.

Using VALGRIND_LIB directly is not supported.

The command that you are using is busybox, not ls. The most likely cause is that your busybox is statically linked and that the Valgrind that you were using was too old to read the symbols for malloc etc from a static binary. The default changed with Valgrind 3.13 (June 2017), well after this question was asked. Older versions of Valgrind should use --soname-synonyms=somalloc=NONE explicitly. There may still be issues with that if the busybox binary is stripped and no debuginfo is available.
